examples: A sponge can absorb water.
The towel absorbs the water on the floor.
Dry dirt absorbs the rain.

more.def: To take in or soak up something, such as a liquid, heat, or light.
examples: Dark clothes absorb more heat from the sun than light clothes.
Plant roots absorb water from the soil.
Thick curtains absorbed most of the noise from the street.

easy.def: Something bad that happens that no one wanted to happen.
examples: I spilled my milk by accident.
There was a car accident on our street.
Dropping the plate was an accident.

more.def: Something that happens by chance and is not planned, often causing harm or damage.
examples: He broke the vase by accident when he bumped the table.
We met by accident at the grocery store.
Wearing a helmet can protect you in a bike accident.

easy.def: To do something you worked hard for.
examples: You can achieve your goal if you keep trying.
He achieved his goal of riding a bike.
I want to achieve a high score.

more.def: To succeed in doing something through effort or skill.
examples: She achieved her dream of swimming across the lake.
The class achieved its goal of reading one hundred books.
You can achieve a lot when you practice every day.

easy.def: To think someone or something is very good.
examples: I admire my big sister.
We admire the pretty rainbow.
I admire how fast you can run.

more.def: To respect and look up to someone, or to enjoy looking at something.
examples: We stopped to admire the colorful sunset.
The students admire their coach for never giving up.
Visitors admired the tall towers of the old castle.

easy.def: A fun and exciting trip or time.
examples: We went on an adventure in the woods.
My book is about an adventure at sea.
Camping in the yard was an adventure.

more.def: An exciting experience, often one that is new or a little bit risky.
examples: Sailing across the lake was the biggest adventure of her summer.
Their first plane ride felt like a great adventure.
The story follows a mouse on an adventure through the city.
I am afraid of the dark.
The kitten is afraid of the vacuum.
Do not be afraid. I am here.

more.def: Feeling fear or worry that something bad might happen.
examples: The puppy was afraid of the loud thunder.
He was afraid to jump off the high diving board.
Many people are afraid of spiders, even small ones.

easy.def: To think the same thing as someone else.
examples: We both agree that pizza is yummy.
Do you agree that dogs are fun?
We agree to take turns.

more.def: To have the same opinion as someone, or to say yes to something.
examples: Everyone agreed that the park was the best place for the picnic.
The two teams agreed on the rules before the game began.
I agree with you that we should leave early.
Mom will allow me to stay up late.
The pool does not allow running.
Dad allowed us to have one more cookie.

more.def: To give permission for someone to do or have something.
examples: The museum does not allow visitors to touch the paintings.
Our teacher allows us to read quietly after a test.
Dogs are not allowed inside the bakery.
The magic trick will amaze you.
Her fast running amazed us.
The big fireworks amaze me.

more.def: To fill someone with great surprise or wonder.
examples: The size of the whale amazed everyone on the boat.
It amazes me how many stars you can see in the desert.
The young chess player amazed the crowd with her skill.
The ancient tree is older than my grandpa.
We saw an ancient castle.
This ancient coin is very old.

more.def: From a time very long ago, often thousands of years in the past.
examples: We saw ancient tools in the museum that people used long ago.
Ancient people painted animals on the walls of caves.
The ancient city was buried under sand for centuries.

easy.def: To say you do not agree, sometimes in a mad way.
examples: My brother and I argue about who goes first.
Do not argue with your sister.
They argue about which show to watch.

more.def: To disagree with someone in words, or to give reasons for what you think.
examples: The two friends began to argue about the rules of the game.
The players argued with the referee about the call.
She argued that recess should be ten minutes longer.

easy.def: A person who goes into space.
examples: The astronaut waved from the rocket.
I want to be an astronaut one day.
The astronaut floats in space.

more.def: A person trained to travel and work in space.
examples: The astronaut lived on the space station for six months.
An astronaut wears a special suit to stay safe outside the ship.
The astronauts fixed the telescope while circling the Earth.
Please pay attention to the teacher.
The clown got our attention with a horn.
Babies need a lot of attention.

more.def: Careful watching, listening, or thinking about something.
examples: The loud noise caught the attention of the whole class.
Pay attention to the signs when you cross the street.
The puppy barked to get its owner's attention.

easy.def: Normal, not big and not small.
examples: He is of average height for his age.
It was an average day at home.
My dog is an average size.

more.def: Usual or ordinary; in the middle, not very high or very low.
examples: An average school day lasts about six hours.
The average bus ride to school takes fifteen minutes.
This winter was colder than an average winter.
